description: Advances: specled.spec_review, specled.package\\n\\nEarmark is marked RETIRED on Hex (deprecated; the retirement notice itself points at MDEx). Any adopter whose verification pipeline runs "mix hex.audit" now fails on specled_ex, because hex.audit exits non-zero on a retired dependency anywhere in the tree and offers no ignore or allowlist mechanism — it takes no flags at all.\\n\\nConfirmed downstream: exoterm adopted specled_ex and its "mix preflight" alias went permanently red at the hex.audit step. Everything else in that gate passes (compile --warnings-as-errors, format, credo --strict, sobelow, dialyzer, 723 tests). Tracked there as exoterm-7xj; exoterm worked around it by reordering hex.audit last so it stops masking the gates after it, but the gate cannot go green until this lands.\\n\\nScope is one call site:\\n- mix.exs — the {:earmark, "~> 1.4"} dep\\n- lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex — a single private helper that renders a markdown string to HTML for the spec.review artifact, calling Earmark.as_html/2 with escape: true and compact_output: false. (Line numbers drift between releases; find it by the Earmark.as_html call.)\\n\\nDeliverable:\\n1. Swap to MDEx at that call site, preserving the safe defaults — HTML escaping must stay on, since the rendered content includes user-authored ADR and spec prose.\\n2. Drop the earmark dep.\\n3. Release, so adopters can re-pin.\\n\\nVerification:\\n- mix hex.audit exits 0 in this repo.\\n- mix spec.review still renders ADR bodies and spec summaries with markdown formatting intact and HTML escaped — the specled_-qm1.11 GitHub-style rendering must not regress.\\n- Downstream smoke: re-pin exoterm to the new ref and confirm mix preflight goes fully green.\\n\\nFound during the exoterm SpecLedEx adoption (2026-08-12).

Summary: Earmark is retired on Hex and mix hex.audit has no ignore mechanism, so
specled_ex made every adopter's audit gate unfixably red. MDEx now renders ADR
prose at the single call site, with the GFM extensions and smart punctuation named
explicitly because they were Earmark defaults and are MDEx opt-ins, and with
escape:true/unsafe:false holding the authored-content safety posture. Diffing both
renderers over this repo's own ADR corpus surfaced two things the docs would not
have: MDEx's escape:true would have leaked five live spec-lint authoring markers
into reader-visible text (fixed by strip_prose_html_comments/1, reusing the segment
split resolve_wikilinks/1 already had), and Earmark had been silently corrupting
shipped prose in three ways that MDEx fixes. The rendering surface previously had
no requirement and no test coverage; specled.spec_review.adr_prose_markdown_surface
now states the contract and four tests cover it through the production seam.
mix hex.audit exits 0.

Not delivered here: the ticket's third verification item (re-pin exoterm, confirm

available from this worktree. Filed as specled_-34w.

Dependency options, checked against Hex on 2026-08-12 — the choice is not as obvious as the retirement notice suggests.

MDEx (what the notice recommends)
- {:mdex, "~> 0.13.5"}. MDEx.to_html/2 is a genuine drop-in for Earmark.as_html/2, so the call site barely changes.
- BUT it is a Rust NIF (a comrak binding). It ships precompiled binaries, but adopters building on an unsupported target need a Rust toolchain. That is a heavier ask than the current pure-Elixir dep for what is a dev/test-only tool.
- Watch the pin: mdex 0.12.5 is ITSELF retired on Hex. A loose pin can land on it and reproduce this exact bug. Pin at or above 0.13.

earmark_parser (lighter, but not a drop-in)
- {:earmark_parser, "~> 1.4"} is NOT retired — latest 1.4.46, actively maintained, and the package ex_doc depends on. Only the `earmark` wrapper was retired.
- Pure Elixir, no NIF, and closest to current output since it is the same parser.
- BUT it only parses: EarmarkParser.as_ast/2 returns an AST. Earmark.as_html/2 is parse + transform, and the transform half lives in the retired package. Taking this route means writing the AST-to-HTML step (or vendoring a small transformer).

Recommendation: MDEx if the NIF is acceptable for a dev-only dep, since it keeps the call site trivial and the escaping semantics easy to preserve. earmark_parser if a pure-Elixir tree matters more than the extra rendering code.

Either way the acceptance criteria are unchanged: mix hex.audit exits 0, and mix spec.review still renders ADR and spec prose with HTML escaping intact (specled_-qm1.11 must not regress).
